newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Croats torch Moslem houses in Bosnian town.
newsitem.headline: Croats torch Moslem houses in Bosnian town.

text.p: Croats destroyed eight houses in the central Bosnian town of Jajce overnight to discourage Moslem refugees from returning, a NATO spokesman said on Wednesday.

"Sadly, I have some initial reports that last night, seven houses were reported burning and an explosion apparently destroyed another in the area," Major John Blakeley of the NATO-led peace force told reporters.
Three days ago, hundreds of Moslems who had moved back to the area after being expelled in wartime were forced to flee by a mob of drunken Croats.

The tensions in Jajce erupted before a meeting in Split on Wednesday between the Moslem chairman of Bosnia's presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman, who is under Western pressure to lean on Bosnian Croats.
Mediators in the office of the international High Representative said they were anxious to prevent harassment in Jajce from derailing a recent positive trend in federation relations.

Small numbers of refugees have been returning to their homes in central Bosnia in recent months, partly because Western governments have promised aid to municipalities which allow minorities back to their communities.

The High Representative's office announced that authorities in the central Bosnian canton -- which includes Jajce -- agreed on Tuesday to form a unified police force that would reflect the mixed ethnic composition of the area.
The agreement should help defuse tensions and enable the return of refugees in a safe manner, a spokesman for the High Representative, Carlos Westendorp, said.

The Dayton peace agreement signed in 1995 guarantees the right of refugees to move back to their pre-war homes. But nationalist authorities, especially Serb leaders, have tended to block the return of refugees who do not belong to the local ethnic majority.
